title: session-capsule-feature-sketch
content:
Quick notes / parking-lot for 'Session Capsule' — a small, per-session metadata container that travels with requests and lets downstream runtime & console make cheap fidelity / routing decisions. Rough PRD brainstorm + user stories and a low-effort rollout path.

Context (why I'm jotting this down):
- We keep circling back to ways to make short-lived, per-user signals (intent, privacy-tier, expected latency tolerance) available to the serving runtime without adding full session state complexity.
- Hosted API customers want a way to attach lightweight hints to requests that persist for the session lifetime and can be used for caching, routing, and fallback policies.
- Private/Dedicated customers want the same surface but with controls for schema and encryption.

Problem statement:
- Current approach: clients pass hints in headers or tokens on every request. This is noisy, error-prone, and harder to reason about consistently (duplicated across SDKs, increases client logic).
- Platform needs a small concept of 'session metadata' that:
  * can be minted by API on first request / created explicitly by client
  * has a short TTL (session lifetime) and is fast to read by router/runtime
  * is editable by the client (with rate limits) and visible in Console for debugging
  * supports a few typed fields we control and an opaque 'tags' bag for users

Goals:
- Developer UX: create a one-line API to create/update/resolve a Session Capsule. Minimal friction to adopt (SDK helpers).
- Runtime: capsules are cheap to attach to requests (in-memory routing table or KV) and do not require heavy serialization each token.
- Console: show capsule snapshot in request trace, allow manual edit for debugging, and optionally persist capsule snapshot to audit logs if customer enables it.

Non-goals:
- Not intended to be a full session-store for long-term conversation history.
- Not a replacement for customer-managed user storage. TTL will be limited (e.g., 24h default).

Proposed capsule schema (starter):
- capsule_id: server-generated UUID (string)
- owner_user_id: (string) optional for console linking
- privacy_tier: enum {public, restricted, sensitive} (affects routing & retention)
- latency_budget_ms: integer (soft hint for routing to low-latency nodes)
- model_preference: string (e.g., "gptx-7b-q4", or alias)
- tags: list<string> freeform short tags
- sticky_kv_refs: list<string> (opaque keys for light prefix cache attachments)
- created_at, last_modified, ttl_seconds

Notes: schema must be intentionally tiny; keep extensible via tags. For Private deployments, an allowlist can lock which fields are writable.

API surface (sketch):
- POST /v1/sessions => { capsule_id, ttl_seconds?, initial_fields? } 201 Created
- GET /v1/sessions/{capsule_id} => capsule snapshot
- PATCH /v1/sessions/{capsule_id} => partial update (field-level RBAC; rate limit 1/s)
- DELETE /v1/sessions/{capsule_id} => expire early
- Optional: header X-Session-Capsule: capsule_id to attach to per-request calls (SDK will set automatically once minted)

SDK ergonomics:
- SDK helpers: client.sessions.create({ttl, initialFields}) returns id; subsequent client.request(...) attaches capsule automatically.
- Auto-mint: first request with 'create: true' can auto-mint a capsule and return capsule_id in response headers if the caller doesn't want to manage lifecycle.

User stories (priority ordered):
1) As an app dev, I want to create a capsule at user sign-in and have it attached to subsequent generation requests so the runtime routes to lower-latency pool for premium users.
   - Acceptance: create + request attach flows work in Node and Python SDKs; Console shows capsule_id on traces.
2) As a platform engineer, I want to query active capsules per deployment to estimate temporary routing load.
   - Acceptance: telemetry endpoint in Console shows active capsule counts and distribution by privacy_tier.
3) As a security reviewer, I want Private customers to be able to mark certain fields as immutable so that downstream services cannot be spoofed.
   - Acceptance: private deploy config supports permitted_writes set; attempts to write blocked fields return 403.
4) As a debugging engineer, I want to edit a capsule in console for a single request re-run so I can reproduce failures caused by different hints.
   - Acceptance: 'Edit Capsule' action in trace opens a quick modal; changes are applied to a new ephemeral capsule used for replay only.

Success metrics (initial):
- 25% of new customers use capsules within first 30 days of SDK update (opt-in telemetry).
- 30% reduction in per-request header noise for integrated clients (measure header size & duplication).
- Positive qualitative feedback from 3 pilot customers on routing improvements.

Runtime considerations / implementation options:
- Option A (fast in-memory): capsules live in a regional in-memory store (Redis) keyed by capsule_id, read by router. TTL enforced by Redis. Fast but requires cross-region replication decision.
- Option B (sticky KV in serving node): store capsule references in the serving node's small KV (fast reads, works well when session affinity exists). Eviction complexity.
- Option C (JWT-like signed capsule): capsule contents encoded & signed; router validates signature and reads fields from header. Zero storage but increases request size and loses editability.

Initial approach suggestion: start with Option A (Redis) for hosted API POC. For Private, allow customers to plug their KVS or use internal in-memory option. Explore signed short tokens for low-trust, high-throughput customers.

Rollout plan (high-level):
- Week 0–2: prototype API + SDK libs in internal branch; demo using sample app (premium-user routing).
- Week 3–5: small pilot with 2 customers + internal SRE load test. Collect feedback on read latency and operational cost.
- Week 6–8: Console integration (trace view, simple editor), docs, and SDK GA; feature flagged.
- Post GA: add private-deploy config options (writable fields allowlist, encryption at rest) and signed-token variant.

Open questions / risks (parking lot):
- How granular should privacy_tier be? Will customers need more than three levels?
- Operational cost: if many customers create millions of capsules/day, can Redis ops scale without becoming a cost sink? Consider TTL batching and write gating.
- Abuse: captions could carry too much PII despite TTL — need redaction/retention policy and Console masking.
- Schema migration: if we add fields later, how to version safely? Consider a 'schema_version' field.

Quick TODOs (for next pass):
- [ ] Draft internal RFC for Redis vs signed tokens with perf numbers (Hiro)
- [ ] Prototype Node SDK auto-mint helper (Oliver)
- [ ] Mock Console trace UI (Mira)
- [ ] Add sample customer use-case docs for pilot (billing + routing)

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep capsule small. Resist adding long JSON blobs — it's tempting but defeats purpose.
- Consider 'capsule templates' in Console for common presets (e.g., "premium-low-latency", "gdpr-strict").
- Could fold into existing session-cookie experiment later; but separate small surface may be easier to ship.

References / related:
- convo-session-ontology (confluence) — links TODO
- JIRA: JIRA-CORE-2109 (related routing task)
- GitHub prototype: session-proto/pull/88 (early impl)

End of sketch. Will iterate once we have a quick perf bench and a UX wire.

-- Oliver
